column1: # Verilog oracle corpus: which independent simulators each case may be
# compared against.
#   <corpus-relative .v path>\t<oracles>\t<note>
# `oracles` is a comma-separated subset of: iverilog, verilator
# Why the column exists. Icarus Verilog is a four-state event simulator and
# Verilator is a two-state cycle simulator, and that is a design decision on
# Verilator's part rather than a deficiency. Where a case's answer depends on X
# or Z the two tools cannot agree, and demanding that they do would make the
# harness report a defect that is not there. Listing the applicable oracles per
# case keeps the oracle-vs-oracle self-check meaningful: a disagreement between
# two listed oracles is always a real finding.
# Every case is deliberately two-state-clean except `xz_propagation.v`, which
# exists precisely to cover the four-state rules and is therefore Icarus-only.
# There is no RSpice contract column yet. Nothing in RSpice executes digital
# Verilog, so every case would carry the same value and the column would be
# scaffolding. It arrives with the CFG interpreter (W2.3), at the same commit
# that removes the harness's `RspiceExecutionUnimplemented` refusal.
c17.v
column3: ISCAS85 c17, exhaustive truth table over five inputs

column1: gate_primitives.v
column3: all eight gate primitives against their operator spellings

column1: ripple_adder.v
column3: 8-bit carry chain, generate-unrolled from full adders

column1: dff_register.v
column3: posedge clocking, asynchronous reset, non-blocking vector update

column1: nba_ordering.v
column3: blocking versus non-blocking, arranged to be defined rather than raced

column1: xz_propagation.v
column3: four-state rules; Verilator is two-state by design and is excluded
